meaning: Managed Slurm: AWS runs the Slurm controller and launches EC2 instances in your account for the jobs you submit.
The job scheduler of high-performance computing: it holds waiting jobs and decides which job gets which machines.
The field that runs simulations and training across many machines at once.
The Slurm process that holds the list of waiting jobs and allocates nodes to them; in PCS, AWS runs it in one of three sizes.
A machine that runs jobs; in PCS, one EC2 instance running slurmd and the PCS agent.
The Slurm daemon on each compute node that takes orders from the controller.
A named Slurm queue in front of a set of nodes; a PCS queue is one partition.
The PCS object users submit jobs to; it is one Slurm partition and points at one or more compute node groups.
The PCS object that says how nodes are created: instance types, minimum and maximum count, subnets, image and one purchase option.
The Slurm command that submits a shell script as a job and returns at once.
The Slurm command that starts a program on every node a job was given.
The Slurm command that lists jobs and their states.
The Slurm command that queries the accounting record of past jobs.
One Slurm submission that expands into many numbered copies of the same script, each scheduled on its own.
How Slurm counts resources that are neither CPU cores nor memory, GPUs above all.
The states squeue shows for a job: waiting, waiting for its nodes to come up, and running.
The opt-in PCS log that records each node as LAUNCHED, REGISTERED, ACTIVE or TERMINATED, with a reason.
How long a node may sit idle before PCS removes it; 600 seconds by default.
Slurm putting a job that lost its node back in the queue, to start again from the top of its script.
A label on a group's nodes and the job option that asks for nodes carrying it; how a job picks a group inside a shared queue.
The always-on machine where users type Slurm commands; in PCS, a static compute node group attached to no queue.
An EC2 object holding instance settings a compute node group cannot express: EFA interfaces, placement group, reservations, user data.
The script an EC2 instance runs at boot; here it mounts the shared file system.
The disk image an EC2 instance boots from.
The EC2 network device that lets processes on different nodes exchange data without passing through the operating system's network stack.
The EC2 placement setting AWS recommends for a compute node group that uses EFA.
A managed parallel file system built for many nodes reading and writing large files at once.
A managed NFS share, used here for home directories.
Your private network in AWS, in which the cluster's nodes run.
The unit EC2 uses to size an instance's processor.
A hold on EC2 instances of one type, so that the capacity is there when a group launches.
A block of GPU instances booked ahead for a fixed window.
A P6e-GB200 or P6e-GB300 machine that joins many GPUs with NVLink.
NVIDIA's direct GPU-to-GPU connection.
The NVIDIA service that lets GPUs in different nodes share memory; on PCS it needs a dedicated domain per job.
A script PCS runs on a node at one of two boot stages: nodeBootstrapped, before slurmd starts, or nodeReady, after.
AWS's other route to a Slurm cluster; its boot hooks map onto PCS node lifecycle actions.
A model trained to predict what the robot's cameras will show next; the multi-node training job of this section's worked case.
